title: Understanding Counterspeech for Online Harm Mitigation
measurement_description: The paper reviews studies that evaluate the effectiveness of counterspeech against specific types of religious-based hate, namely Islamophobia and Islamic extremism. It also examines counterspeech designed to challenge Islamist extremist recruitment narratives and the impact of such interventions on Muslim bystanders.
findings: The review finds that Islamophobia and Islamic extremism are among the most commonly addressed phenomena in counterspeech research. Studies have been conducted to evaluate strategies for countering Islamist extremist narratives and to understand the effects of counterspeech on Muslim in-group bystanders' intention to intervene.
